RFC3768-5.2.3-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 5.2.3 says "The TTL MUST be set to 255." TestSendAdvertIPv4HeaderTTLProtoDst changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same. It still compares the TTL octet of the built IPv4 header with the literal 255, single-polarity per the row annotation. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-5.2.3-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 5.2.3 says "A VRRP router receiving a packet with the TTL not equal to 255 MUST discard the packet." TestDecodeGoldenV2 lost only the assertion on the removed MsgOnlyChecksum flag, which carried no RFC 3768 content, and TestNegativeReferenceBugs gained the FillChecksum mode argument and an rfc5798-compatible lookup in N1 alone; verifyReceived returns before any mode is read for version 2, so the VRRPv2 decode under judgement is unchanged. TestDecodeV2DiscardsTTLNot255 still accepts the VRRPv2 golden at TTL 255 and refuses TTL 0/1/64/254 with ErrTTL. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-5.3.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 5.3.2 says "A packet with unknown type MUST be discarded." TestDecodeGoldenV2 lost only the assertion on the removed MsgOnlyChecksum flag, which carried no RFC 3768 content, and TestNegativeReferenceBugs gained the FillChecksum mode argument and an rfc5798-compatible lookup in N1 alone; verifyReceived returns before any mode is read for version 2, so the VRRPv2 decode under judgement is unchanged. TestDecodeV2DiscardsUnknownType still refuses Type 0, 2 and 15 with ErrType over a recomputed checksum. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-5.3.4-1.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestV2OwnerRunsAtPriority255 extracts a group with version 2 and fatals unless Version reached the spec as v2; the owner configured at 120 must have EffectivePriority 255 under decrements 0, 1, 119 and 4064 and must advertise Priority 255 on startup; a v2 non-owner keeps 120 (negative). Records: revert EffectivePriority, both polarities, observed red.

RFC3768-5.3.4-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestV2BoundaryPriority validates version-2 groups (version asserted at extraction): 1 and 254 accepted, 0 and 255 refused with the range-check text 'is out of range; configure 1..254' (so no other check can satisfy the case), and a v2 non-owner at 100 floors at 1 under decrements 99, 100, 4064. Records: revert validateGroup, both polarities.

RFC3768-5.3.6-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 5.3.6 says "A packet with unknown authentication type or that does not match the locally configured authentication method MUST be discarded." TestDecodeGoldenV2 lost only the assertion on the removed MsgOnlyChecksum flag, which carried no RFC 3768 content, and TestNegativeReferenceBugs gained the FillChecksum mode argument and an rfc5798-compatible lookup in N1 alone; verifyReceived returns before any mode is read for version 2, so the VRRPv2 decode under judgement is unchanged. Auth Type 1, 2, 3, 128 and 255 are still each refused with ErrAuthType and Auth Type 0 accepted. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-6.4.2-1.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Re-read: the unit's body is unchanged; only the 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 Virtual Router MAC proxy tags left it for TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames, so the verdict stands. Prior note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): Forbidden: a v2 Backup answering ARP for the virtual address. TestV2BackupHoldsNoVirtualAddress starts a Version 2 non-owner, requires Backup, zero address installs and no acceptance filter; the v2 owner contrast is Master with exactly one install on the virtual-MAC device. Asserted at Ze's boundary (the address Ze installs for the kernel ARP responder), the lower-layer form ai/rules/rfc-compliance.md asks for; no ARP is observed on the wire. Records: revert doInstallVIPs, both polarities. The Backup's virtual-MAC macvlan is up (D-8) but holds no address, so it has nothing to answer for.

RFC3768-6.4.2-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuation 3): Wiring now proven on the host: TestBackupDiscardFollowsTheState drives the FSM and asserts the worker sets the discard on the virtual router MAC device at start (idle worker: on then off), entering Backup adds no call, promotion withdraws it once after the only install, and a higher-priority advert demotes and sets it again before the only removal (records observed red on doRemoveVIPs; the run revert was also observed red but the ledger keeps one record per unit/polarity). Wire effect: TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames (QEMU guest) forwards a transit datagram sent to the Virtual Router MAC without the nft drop and stops it with it (records on backupFilterTables). The host unit's negative tag is a state contrast; the violating negative (no discard, frame forwarded) is the QEMU control.

RFC3768-6.4.2-3.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Re-read: the unit's body is unchanged; only the 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 Virtual Router MAC proxy tags left it for TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames, so the verdict stands. Prior note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): Forbidden: a v2 Backup accepting packets addressed to the virtual address. Same unit as 6.4.2-1: a Version 2 Backup installs no address (so the kernel has no local route for it) and hands no acceptance filter; the v2 Master contrast installs it. Records: revert doInstallVIPs, both polarities. Forwarding of virtual-MAC frames by a Backup is the separate RFC3768-6.4.2-2 defect (D-8), not this row.

RFC3768-6.4.2-4.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestV2BackupShutdown runs a VRRPv2 Backup: Shutdown yields exactly [StopTimers, Backup->Initialize] and state Initialize; the canceled timer's later expiry does nothing. The exact action list pins both the cancel and the transition.

RFC3768-6.4.2-5.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestPromotionSetsAdverTimerToOwnInterval: a VRRPv2 Backup's live expiry yields exactly SendAdvert{100,2000}, InstallVIPs, AnnounceFailover, StartAdvertTimer{2s}, Backup->Master; an unarmed generation promotes nothing. TestAnnounceMasterFramesPerAddress checks each announced frame against literals: broadcast ARP request per VIP, sender and target hardware address 00-00-5e-00-01-0a, target protocol address the VIP, exactly the VIP set.

RFC3768-6.4.2-6.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestV2BackupPriorityZeroSetsSkewTime: Priority 0 arms the literal 0.609375 s ((256-100)/256, not the v3 1.21875 s); non-zero Priority 1 arms the literal 6.609375 s Master_Down_Interval. Expectations no longer come from skewTime.

RFC3768-6.4.2-7.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestV2BackupResetsOrDiscards on VRRPv2: equal, greater and Preempt-off lower each arm the literal local 6.609375 s and stay Backup; Preempt-on lower produces nothing and the earlier timer still promotes. No interval adoption is asserted for v2 (the old wrong v3 row is no longer the evidence).

RFC3768-6.4.2-8.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): Same unit as RFC3768-6.4.2-7: the greater-priority case is now fed, so an '==' comparison fails; the discard branch is proven by no action plus the old timer still promoting.

RFC3768-6.4.3-1.note: vrrp closure judge 2026-09-30 (independent) re-judged: the tagged units changed only by added RFC requirement tag comment lines for the new rows (8.1.2-6 / 8.2.2-8 / 8.2-4 / 8.1.1-2); test bodies byte-identical, records current, verdict unchanged. Prior note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuation 3): Product install now proven: TestPromotionInstallsIPv4AddressOnVirtualMACDevice (v2 subtest) asserts a Backup installs nothing and the promoted non-owner makes exactly one install, on the virtual-MAC macvlan zv4-2-10 (never the parent), of exactly 192.0.2.1/24 (record observed red on doInstallVIPs). TestVRRPNonOwnerMasterAnswersARPWithVirtualMACOnly (QEMU guest) proves that installed state answers ARP and that no reply is seen with the address removed (records on vipCIDRs). The dataplane_linux_test sysctl tags stay without records.

RFC3768-6.4.3-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuation 3): Wiring now proven on the host: TestBackupDiscardFollowsTheState asserts promotion withdraws the discard exactly once and only after the address install, and that it holds before promotion and after demotion (records observed red on doInstallVIPs and doRemoveVIPs). Wire effect: TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames (QEMU guest) forwards the datagram sent to the Virtual Router MAC once the filter is withdrawn and the address installed, and not while the filter holds (records on clearBackupFilter).

RFC3768-6.4.3-3.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 re-read after RFC3768-6.4.3-4 tags were added to TestActiveV2RouterAcceptsOnlyWhenItOwnsTheAddress (body unchanged): Forbidden: a v2 non-owner Master accepting packets addressed to the virtual address. The Version 2 test fatals unless exactly one accept-filter call is made and errors unless accept=false for the non-owner and accept=true for the owner.

RFC3768-6.4.3-4.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Re-read: the unit's body is unchanged; only the 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 Virtual Router MAC proxy tags left it for TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames, so the verdict stands. Prior note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestActiveV2RouterAcceptsOnlyWhenItOwnsTheAddress promotes a Version 2 group to Master and requires exactly one acceptance-filter call with accept=true for the owner (positive) and accept=false for the non-owner (negative), so an owner suppression or an acceptance granted to every Master goes red. Records: revert EffectiveAcceptMode, both polarities. The older tags on TestInstanceOwnerStartupGoesMaster/NonOwnerGoesBackup remain and add nothing.

RFC3768-6.4.3-5.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestV2MasterShutdown: a Version 2 owner Master receives Shutdown; the last advert carries Priority 0, state is Initialize, in.advert is nil, and after 10 s of fake clock no timer event and no further advert appear (Cancel Adver_Timer, Send Priority 0, Transition to Initialize, each asserted). Contrast: a v2 Backup shutting down sends nothing. Records: revert cancelTimers, both polarities. The FSM matrix row master/shutdown still runs v3.

RFC3768-6.4.3-6.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestV2MasterAdverTimerFires on VRRPv2: the live expiry yields exactly SendAdvert{100,2000}, StartAdvertTimer{2s}; an unarmed generation yields nothing.

RFC3768-6.4.3-7.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestV2MasterPriorityZero on VRRPv2: Priority 0 yields exactly SendAdvert{100,2000}, StartAdvertTimer{2s} and stays Master; a non-zero lower-priority advert yields nothing.

RFC3768-6.4.3-8.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): the previously missing v2 'Priority greater' clause is now TestV2MasterYieldsToAHigherPriority: a Version 2 Master (source 192.0.2.2) gets Priority 250 from the LOWER sender 192.0.2.1, so only priority decides; it must be Backup, in.advert nil, silent for two intervals, Backup at MDI-1ms and Master at MDI+1ms with MDI = 3 s + 56/256 s (RFC 3768 6.1); a Priority 150 advert from the greater 192.0.2.8 holds Master with the timer armed (negative). Records: revert demoteToBackup, both polarities. The equal-priority tie-break clause stays proven by TestInstanceTieBreakComparesTheAdvertisementSource and TestInstanceV2TieBreakDemotionRestartsTheTimers (records syncSourceLocked, senderWinsTieBreak, demoteToBackup).

RFC3768-6.4.3-9.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): TestV2MasterDemotesOrDiscards on VRRPv2: higher priority and equal priority from 192.0.2.200 (greater than .10 only unsigned) each yield exactly StopTimers, RemoveVIPs, StartMasterDownTimer{6.609375s literal}, Master->Backup; equal from a smaller sender and lower priority yield nothing and stay Master.

RFC3768-7.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.1 says "MUST verify the VRRP version is 2." TestDecodeGoldenV2 lost only the assertion on the removed MsgOnlyChecksum flag, which carried no RFC 3768 content, and TestNegativeReferenceBugs gained the FillChecksum mode argument and an rfc5798-compatible lookup in N1 alone; verifyReceived returns before any mode is read for version 2, so the VRRPv2 decode under judgement is unchanged. N9 still requires ErrVersion for a v3 packet at a v2 group and the reverse; the v2 golden decodes. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-7.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.1 says "MUST verify that the received packet contains the complete VRRP packet (including fixed fields, IP Address(es), and Authentication Data)." TestDecodeGoldenV2 lost only the assertion on the removed MsgOnlyChecksum flag, which carried no RFC 3768 content, and TestNegativeReferenceBugs gained the FillChecksum mode argument and an rfc5798-compatible lookup in N1 alone; verifyReceived returns before any mode is read for version 2, so the VRRPv2 decode under judgement is unchanged. Cuts inside the fixed fields still return ErrTruncated and short Authentication Data or address lists ErrLength; the complete golden is accepted. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-7.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.1 says "MUST verify the VRRP checksum." TestDecodeGoldenV2 lost only the assertion on the removed MsgOnlyChecksum flag, which carried no RFC 3768 content, and TestNegativeReferenceBugs gained the FillChecksum mode argument and an rfc5798-compatible lookup in N1 alone; verifyReceived returns before any mode is read for version 2, so the VRRPv2 decode under judgement is unchanged. TestDecodeV2ChecksumCorrupt still requires ErrChecksum on a flipped v2 checksum, and the golden G1 still verifies as a message-only sum. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-7.1-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.1 says "MUST verify that the VRID is configured on the receiving interface and the local router is not the IP Address owner (Priority equals 255 (decimal))." TestDecodeGoldenV2 lost only the assertion on the removed MsgOnlyChecksum flag, which carried no RFC 3768 content, and TestNegativeReferenceBugs gained the FillChecksum mode argument and an rfc5798-compatible lookup in N1 alone; verifyReceived returns before any mode is read for version 2, so the VRRPv2 decode under judgement is unchanged. TestRxAdvertScopedToReceivingInterface changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same, so the VRID 10 advert sent on the VRID-20 interface is still refused with ErrUnknownVRID and arrives on its own interface. Verdict unchanged; its discrimination records read unit-changed and need re-recording in the guest.

RFC3768-7.1-5.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.1 says "MUST verify that the Auth Type matches the locally configured authentication method for the virtual router and perform that authentication method." TestDecodeGoldenV2 lost only the assertion on the removed MsgOnlyChecksum flag, which carried no RFC 3768 content, and TestNegativeReferenceBugs gained the FillChecksum mode argument and an rfc5798-compatible lookup in N1 alone; verifyReceived returns before any mode is read for version 2, so the VRRPv2 decode under judgement is unchanged. N8 still requires ErrAuthType for Auth Type 1; the golden type 0 decodes. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-7.1-6.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.1 says "If any one of the above checks fails, the receiver MUST discard the packet". TestInstanceRxValidAdvertReachesFSM changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same. The per-check discard proof in TestInstanceRxFailedCheckIsDiscarded is unchanged, and an overlay mutant making instance.lookup hand Decode the rfc5798-compatible mode reddened that test and TestInstanceRxValidAdvertReachesFSM, so the receive path still reaches the checks. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-7.1-7.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.1 says "If the packet was not generated by the address owner (Priority does not equal 255 (decimal)), the receiver MUST drop the packet, otherwise continue processing." The cited producer onPacket changed only by deleting the MsgOnlyChecksum counter block that ran after a successful Decode; the version 2 address-list comparison, the drop for a sender Priority other than 255 and the continue for Priority 255 are untouched. The three address-list tests still pin drop, continue and match. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-7.1-8.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.1 says "MUST verify that the Adver Interval in the packet is the same as the locally configured for this virtual router". TestDecodeGoldenV2 lost only the assertion on the removed MsgOnlyChecksum flag, which carried no RFC 3768 content, and TestNegativeReferenceBugs gained the FillChecksum mode argument and an rfc5798-compatible lookup in N1 alone; verifyReceived returns before any mode is read for version 2, so the VRRPv2 decode under judgement is unchanged. The interval-mismatch cases still require ErrV2IntervalMismatch; the golden with the equal interval decodes. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-7.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.2 says "Fill in the VRRP packet fields with the appropriate virtual router configuration state - Compute the VRRP checksum". TestEncodeGoldenV2 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument, and FillChecksum seeds a pseudo-header only when the version nibble is 3, so the VRRPv2 encode still has to equal the golden G1 byte for byte, checksum 0x92ED included. Single-polarity positive. Verdict unchanged.

RFC3768-7.2-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.2 says "Set the source MAC address to Virtual Router MAC Address". TestTxAdvertV4OnWire changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same; the captured VRRPv2 source MAC is still compared with 00-00-5e-00-01-0a. Verdict unchanged; the guest-only discrimination record reads unit-changed and is owed a re-record under QEMU.

RFC3768-7.2-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.2 says "Set the source IP address to interface primary IP address". TestTxAdvertV4OnWire changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same; the captured VRRPv2 source must still be the primary 192.0.2.251 over a lower secondary. Verdict unchanged; the guest-only discrimination record reads unit-changed and is owed a re-record under QEMU.

RFC3768-7.2-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 3768 Section 7.2 says "Set the IP protocol to VRRP - Send the VRRP packet to the VRRP IP multicast group".
